person.name: Sedona Thomas
intro: Full-stack developer with 3+ years of experience building containerized microservices in Java and monitoring cloud-native applications with Prometheus and Grafana.
bio: Full-stack developer specializing in cloud-native Java Spring Boot microservices in high-complexity environments. Columbia University graduate with a dual-B.A./B.S. in Computer Science and Human Rights. Strong experience with microservice observability in cloud-native environments.

Prior roles include leading automated integration testing and application monitoring efforts across a suite of containerized microservices, specifically through the design of intuitive, user-friendly Grafana dashboards for use by both service developers and non-technical maintainers.

courses.title: University Writing - Human Rights
courses.description: University Writing helps undergraduates engage in the conversations that form our intellectual community. By reading and writing about scholarly and popular essays, students learn that writing is a process of continual refinement of ideas. Rather than approaching writing as an innate talent, this course teaches writing as a learned skill. We give special attention to textual analysis, research, and revision practices. University Writing offers the following themed sections, all of which welcome students with no prior experience studying the theme. Students interested in a particular theme should register for the section within the specified range of section numbers. (UW: Readings in Human Rights (sections in the 400s). Features essays that investigate the ethics of belonging to a community and issues of personhood, identity, representation, and action.)

courses.title: The Art of Engineering
courses.description: This course is a bridge between the science-oriented, high school way of thinking and the engineering point of view. Fundamental concepts of math and science are reviewed and re-framed in an engineering context, with numerous examples of each concept drawn from all disciplines of engineering represented at Columbia. Non-technical issues of importance in professional engineering practice such as ethics, engineering project management, and societal impact are addressed.

courses.title: Physics I: Mechanics/Relativity
courses.description: Fundamental laws of mechanics, kinematics and dynamics, work and energy, rotational dynamics, oscillations, gravitation, fluids, introduction to special relativity and relativistic kinematics. The course is preparatory for advanced work in physics and related fields.

courses.title: General Chemistry I
courses.description: Topics include stoichiometry, states of matter, nuclear properties, electronic structures of atoms, periodic properties, chemical bonding, molecular geometry, introduction to quantum mechanics and atomic theory, introduction to organic and biological chemistry, solid state and materials science, polymer science and macromolecular structures and coordination chemistry. Although CHEM UN1403 and CHEM UN1404 are separate courses, students are expected to take both terms sequentially. The order of presentation of topics may differ from the order presented here, and from year to year. Students must ensure they register for the recitation that corresponds to the lecture section.

Volunteered as a Makerspace staff member and served as a Columbia Health Peer Ambassador.

experience.summary: Full-Stack Software Engineer who developed and monitored scalable backend services using Java and Spring Boot, leveraging Prometheus and Grafana for performance monitoring and observability.
achievements: Maintain a Top-Secret security clearance and ensure federal security protocol compliance
Led the maintenance and expansion of automated integration testing and observability for seven Kafka-based microservices.
Built Grafana dashboards for real-time monitoring of system metrics via Prometheus and automated test reporting via InfluxDB.
Founded and led weekly cross-team testing meetings to improve collaboration and knowledge sharing within an Agile/Scrum development team.
Enhanced a Dockerized Java Spring Boot microservice responsible for processing high-volume XML messages through Kafka.
Maintained and expanded a comprehensive suite of automated Python integration tests using Pytest, improving test coverage and software reliability.
Integrated Drools rule workflows, REST APIs, and GeoServer data to support real-time alerts and automated responses.
Supported monthly write-ups as an Ethical Legal and Social Implications (ELSI) Liaison for the use of automated decision makers in a foundational research project.

experience.summary: Software Engineering Intern at Amazon Prime Video who developed a proof-of-concept promotional content page using Kotlin and Java.

Implemented backend components while adhering to established engineering and code-quality standards.
Collaborated with software engineers and product managers throughout the feature development process.
Tested and debugged features, resolving issues to improve reliability and performance.
Participated in code reviews, technical discussions, and Agile development processes throughout the feature lifecycle.

experience.summary: Primary course instructor for online 10-week courses teaching AI/ML/NLP to young students.

Taught courses over Zoom ranging from beginner to advanced consisting of elementary through high-school students.
Led development of course materials integrating technology ethics discussions.

experience.summary: Volunteer makerspace staff member leading equipment trainings and holding open hours to assist users with fabrication tools and projects.

Led hands-on workshops on leathercraft, stained glass, jewelry smithing, 3D printing, laser cutting, and electronics.
Trained and advised students, researchers, and community members on equipment use, prototyping techniques, and makerspace policies.
Assisted with troubleshooting, workspace organization, equipment maintenance, and enforcement of health and safety procedures.
Collaborated with makers from diverse technical backgrounds to develop projects, share knowledge, and foster an inclusive creative environment.
Promoted responsible tool use and independent problem-solving while serving as a knowledgeable point of contact during open hours.
